name: Back pain
summary: Back pain is very common and usually improves within a few weeks. Staying active is one of the best things you can do.
redFlags: Numbness or tingling around the genitals or bottom
Difficulty peeing, being unable to pee, or losing control of your bladder or bowels
Weakness or numbness in both legs, or being unsteady on your feet
Back pain with chest pain, or sudden severe back pain with fainting
Back pain after a serious fall or accident
urgentFlags: Back pain with a high temperature or feeling unwell
Back pain with numbness, weakness or pins and needles in one leg that is getting worse
Pain that is getting worse quickly, or is severe at night or at rest
Back pain with unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer
Swelling or a change in the shape of your back

commonCauses.title: Muscle or ligament strain
commonCauses.detail: Often after lifting, twisting or awkward movement; the most common cause.

commonCauses.title: Sciatica
commonCauses.detail: Pain shooting down the leg from an irritated nerve in the lower back.

commonCauses.title: Wear and tear
commonCauses.detail: Age-related changes in the spine, which are very common and often cause no pain.

commonCauses.title: Posture and inactivity
commonCauses.detail: Long periods sitting or poor working positions.

commonCauses.title: Kidney infection or other causes
commonCauses.detail: Pain in the side or back with a high temperature can come from the kidneys.

selfCare: Keep moving and continue normal activities as much as you can
Take ibuprofen or paracetamol, following the pack instructions
Use heat packs or cold packs to ease pain
Try gentle back stretches and exercise such as walking, swimming or yoga
Sleep on your side with a pillow between your knees
avoid: Bed rest for more than a day or two
Heavy lifting until pain eases
Sitting for long periods without moving
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after a few weeks
Pain stops you doing day-to-day activities
Pain is very bad or getting worse over time
You are worried about the pain or struggling to cope

name: Pain shooting down the leg (sciatica)
summary: Sciatica is pain, tingling or numbness that travels from the lower back down the leg, caused by an irritated nerve. It usually gets better within 4 to 6 weeks.
redFlags: Sciatica in both legs
Numbness around or under your genitals, or around your bottom
Difficulty peeing, being unable to pee, or losing control of your bladder or bowels
Severe or worsening weakness in both legs, making it hard to walk
urgentFlags: Increasing numbness or weakness in one leg or foot
Pain so severe it cannot be controlled with pharmacy painkillers
Sciatica with a high temperature or unexplained weight loss

commonCauses.title: Slipped (herniated) disc
commonCauses.detail: A disc in the spine bulges and presses on a nerve; the most common cause.

commonCauses.title: Spinal stenosis
commonCauses.detail: Narrowing of the spinal canal, more common in older people, often worse when walking.

commonCauses.title: Muscle tightness
commonCauses.detail: Tight muscles in the buttock can irritate the nerve.

selfCare: Keep active and keep doing your normal activities as much as possible
Do gentle stretches for sciatica
Use heat packs on the painful area
Take ibuprofen or paracetamol, following the pack instructions
avoid: Sitting or lying down for long periods
Heavy lifting
Putting a hot water bottle directly on the skin, which can burn
seeDoctorIf: Sciatica has not improved after a few weeks
The pain is getting worse or stopping you doing normal activities
You are struggling to cope

name: Neck pain
summary: Neck pain and stiffness are common and usually caused by posture, sleeping awkwardly or muscle strain. They usually improve within a few weeks.
redFlags: A stiff neck with a high temperature and headache, sensitivity to light, or a rash that does not fade under a glass
Neck pain after a fall, car accident or blow to the head
Neck pain with weakness, numbness or loss of coordination in the arms or legs
Sudden severe neck pain with a sudden severe headache
urgentFlags: Neck pain with pins and needles or weakness in one arm
Neck pain with a high temperature and feeling unwell
Severe pain that is getting worse
A lump in the neck that is getting bigger

commonCauses.title: Posture and muscle strain
commonCauses.detail: Working at a computer, looking down at a phone, or sleeping in an awkward position.

commonCauses.title: Wear and tear
commonCauses.detail: Age-related changes in the neck joints and discs.

commonCauses.title: Trapped nerve
commonCauses.detail: Pain spreading into the arm with tingling or numbness.

commonCauses.title: Whiplash
commonCauses.detail: Neck injury after a sudden jolt, such as in a car accident.

selfCare: Keep your neck moving gently; do not use a neck collar
Take ibuprofen or paracetamol, following the pack instructions
Use a heat pack or a cold pack for short periods
Use a low, firm pillow and check your posture at desks and screens
avoid: Wearing a neck collar unless advised by a doctor
Sudden, forceful neck movements or manipulation
Long periods looking down at screens
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after a few weeks
Pain is severe or getting worse
You have pins and needles, numbness or weakness in your arms or hands
Pain is stopping you doing your normal activities

name: Shoulder pain
summary: Shoulder pain is common and is usually caused by a strained muscle or tendon. It often gets better within 2 weeks with rest and gentle movement.
redFlags: Shoulder or left arm pain with chest pain, breathlessness, sweating or feeling sick
Shoulder-tip pain with severe tummy pain, or in early pregnancy
A shoulder that has changed shape or that you cannot move after an injury, with severe pain
Pins and needles or numbness in the arm that does not go away after an injury
urgentFlags: A hot, red, swollen shoulder with a high temperature
Sudden severe pain and being unable to lift the arm
Severe pain that does not improve with painkillers

commonCauses.title: Rotator cuff or tendon problems
commonCauses.detail: Pain when lifting the arm, often from overuse or a strain.

commonCauses.title: Frozen shoulder
commonCauses.detail: Pain and stiffness that gradually make it hard to move the shoulder; more common in middle age.

commonCauses.title: Arthritis
commonCauses.detail: Ongoing pain and stiffness, often in older people.

commonCauses.title: Referred pain
commonCauses.detail: Pain can be felt in the shoulder from the neck, heart or tummy.

selfCare: Rest the shoulder from activities that make the pain worse, but keep it moving gently
Take ibuprofen or paracetamol, following the pack instructions
Use a cold pack for a new injury or heat for ongoing stiffness
Try gentle shoulder exercises and stretches
avoid: Keeping the arm completely still for long periods
Lifting heavy objects or reaching overhead while it hurts
Sleeping on the painful side
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
It is very hard to move your arm or shoulder
Pain started after a fall or injury
You have pins and needles that do not go away

name: Knee pain
summary: Knee pain is common and is often caused by a strain, sprain or wear and tear. Most knee pain improves within a few weeks with self-care.
redFlags: Being unable to put any weight on your leg after an injury
A knee that has changed shape or is badly deformed after an injury
A knee that is hot, red and swollen with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: A red, hot, swollen knee
A knee that is very swollen or locked so you cannot straighten it
Severe pain after a fall or sporting injury
Numbness, tingling, or a cold, pale foot below the painful knee

commonCauses.title: Sprains and strains
commonCauses.detail: Overstretching ligaments or muscles, often during sport.

commonCauses.title: Osteoarthritis
commonCauses.detail: Pain and stiffness, especially in older adults, worse after activity.

commonCauses.title: Cartilage or ligament tear
commonCauses.detail: Pain after a twisting injury, with swelling, locking or giving way.

commonCauses.title: Tendon problems
commonCauses.detail: Pain around the kneecap from overuse, for example in runners.

commonCauses.title: Gout or infection
commonCauses.detail: A hot, red, swollen joint needs prompt assessment.

selfCare: Rest the knee and raise it when you can
Put a cold pack wrapped in a towel on it for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes
Return to gentle activity gradually as pain eases
avoid: Kneeling and activities that strain the knee until it improves
Heat or massage on a new injury for the first 2 to 3 days
Stopping all movement for a long time
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
The knee keeps clicking, locking or giving way
Swelling keeps coming back
Pain is stopping you doing your normal activities

name: Hip pain
summary: Hip pain is often caused by strained muscles, tendon problems or arthritis, and usually improves with rest and gentle exercise. A fall in an older person with hip pain needs urgent assessment.
redFlags: Being unable to stand or put weight on the leg after a fall
The leg is shorter or turned outwards after a fall
Hip pain with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: A hot, swollen hip or groin with a high temperature
Severe pain that started suddenly
A child with hip pain or a limp and a high temperature

commonCauses.title: Muscle strain or tendon problems
commonCauses.detail: Pain on the outer hip, often worse lying on that side.

commonCauses.title: Osteoarthritis
commonCauses.detail: Pain in the groin or hip with stiffness, more common in older people.

commonCauses.title: Referred pain from the back
commonCauses.detail: Back problems can cause pain felt in the hip or buttock.

commonCauses.title: Hip fracture
commonCauses.detail: In older people, after a fall, especially with thin bones (osteoporosis).

selfCare: Rest and avoid activities that make it worse, but keep gently active
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Lose weight if you are overweight, to reduce load on the hip
Wear flat, comfortable shoes
Put a pillow between your knees when lying on your side
avoid: Standing for long periods
Sleeping on the painful side
High-impact exercise until it improves
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
Pain is stopping you doing normal activities
Pain is getting worse or keeps coming back
Pain is worse at night or affecting your sleep

name: Pain and stiffness in several joints
summary: Aching joints are common, especially with age or after a viral illness. Joints that are swollen, warm or stiff for more than 30 minutes in the morning should be checked.
redFlags: A single joint that is suddenly hot, red, very swollen and painful, with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: A hot, red, swollen joint, especially if you cannot move it
Joint pain with a high temperature or a rash
Joint pain after a recent sexually transmitted infection, tummy upset or tick bite

commonCauses.title: Osteoarthritis
commonCauses.detail: Pain and stiffness, usually in the knees, hips and hands, worse after activity.

commonCauses.title: Viral infection
commonCauses.detail: Aching joints during or after flu and other viruses, usually settling within a few weeks.

commonCauses.title: Rheumatoid or other inflammatory arthritis
commonCauses.detail: Swollen, warm joints with stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes in the morning.

commonCauses.title: Gout
commonCauses.detail: Sudden, very painful, red, swollen joint, often the big toe.

commonCauses.title: Overuse
commonCauses.detail: Repetitive movements at work or in sport.

selfCare: Keep active with gentle, low-impact exercise such as walking, swimming or cycling
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, or use an anti-inflammatory gel, following the pack instructions
Use heat for stiffness or cold packs for swelling
Lose weight if you are overweight
avoid: Long periods of inactivity
Supplements such as glucosamine or magnetic bracelets, which have little evidence of benefit
seeDoctorIf: Joint pain has lasted more than 2 weeks
Your joints are swollen or stiff for more than 30 minutes after waking
Pain is affecting your daily life or sleep
You also feel tired or generally unwell

name: Sudden hot, swollen joint
summary: A single joint that suddenly becomes hot, red, swollen and very painful is often gout, but a joint infection must be ruled out quickly.
redFlags: A hot, swollen joint with a high temperature, shivering and feeling very unwell or confused
A hot, swollen joint after recent joint surgery, an injection or with an artificial joint, and feeling unwell
urgentFlags: A joint that is suddenly hot, red, swollen and very painful
Being unable to move the joint
A first episode of suspected gout

commonCauses.title: Gout
commonCauses.detail: Uric acid crystals cause sudden, severe pain, often in the big toe, foot, ankle or knee.

commonCauses.title: Septic arthritis
commonCauses.detail: A joint infection, which is a medical emergency.

commonCauses.title: Pseudogout
commonCauses.detail: Crystals of a different type, often in the knee of older people.

commonCauses.title: Injury
commonCauses.detail: Bleeding into the joint after a knock or twist.

selfCare: Get medical advice the same day, especially for a first episode
Rest and raise the joint
Keep it cool with a cold pack wrapped in a towel
Drink plenty of water
avoid: Alcohol, especially beer, and large amounts of red meat, offal or seafood if you have gout
Putting weight or pressure on the joint
Aspirin for gout pain
seeDoctorIf: You have had gout attacks before and they are becoming more frequent
Swelling has not gone down after treatment
You have lumps on your joints or ears

name: Muscle cramps
summary: Muscle cramps are sudden, painful tightening of a muscle, often in the calf at night. They are usually harmless and last a few minutes.
redFlags: Calf pain with swelling, warmth and redness and sudden breathlessness or chest pain
Severe muscle pain with very dark or brown pee and weakness
urgentFlags: Cramp-like calf pain with swelling, warmth or redness in one leg
Cramps with numbness, weakness or changes in sensation
Cramps after starting a new medicine, with muscle weakness or dark pee

commonCauses.title: Unknown cause
commonCauses.detail: Most night cramps have no clear cause and become more common with age.

commonCauses.title: Exercise and dehydration
commonCauses.detail: Overworked muscles and losing fluid through sweating.

commonCauses.title: Pregnancy
commonCauses.detail: Leg cramps are common in later pregnancy.

commonCauses.title: Medicines and medical conditions
commonCauses.detail: Diuretics, statins, nerve or kidney problems can cause cramps.

selfCare: Stretch and massage the muscle during a cramp, for example pulling your toes towards you for a calf cramp
Do regular calf stretches, especially before bed
Drink enough fluids during exercise and in hot weather
Paracetamol or ibuprofen can ease soreness afterwards, following the pack instructions
avoid: Quinine-containing tonic water as a treatment, which has little benefit
Unproven supplements sold for cramps
seeDoctorIf: Cramps happen often and disturb your sleep
Cramps last more than 10 minutes
You also have numbness, swelling or muscle weakness
You think a medicine is causing them

name: Muscle aches
summary: Aching muscles are usually caused by exercise, tension or a viral illness such as flu, and get better within a few days.
redFlags: Muscle aches with a high temperature, confusion, fast breathing or cold, blotchy skin
Muscle aches with a rash that does not fade when pressed under a glass
Severe muscle pain with very dark or brown pee
urgentFlags: Muscle pain with weakness, especially after starting a new medicine
Muscle aches with a tick bite and a spreading rash
Muscle pain with a stiff neck or severe headache

commonCauses.title: Exercise or overuse
commonCauses.detail: Delayed soreness 1 to 2 days after unaccustomed activity.

commonCauses.title: Viral illness
commonCauses.detail: Flu, COVID-19 and other viruses commonly cause body aches.

commonCauses.title: Stress and tension
commonCauses.detail: Tight muscles, especially in the neck and shoulders.

commonCauses.title: Medicines
commonCauses.detail: Some medicines, such as statins, can cause muscle pain.

commonCauses.title: Long-term conditions
commonCauses.detail: Fibromyalgia, polymyalgia rheumatica, thyroid problems or low vitamin D.

selfCare: Rest and drink plenty of fluids if you have a viral illness
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Use a warm bath or heat pack to ease aches
Gentle stretching and gradual return to exercise
avoid: Intense exercise while you have a fever
Stopping a prescribed medicine without talking to your doctor
seeDoctorIf: Muscle aches last more than 2 weeks
You have muscle weakness
You are over 50 with new pain and stiffness in the shoulders and hips
You think a medicine is causing the pain

name: Swollen ankles, feet or legs
summary: Swelling in the ankles, feet and legs is often caused by fluid building up from standing or sitting for a long time, hot weather or pregnancy. It usually goes away on its own.
redFlags: Swelling with sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing up blood
Swelling in one leg with chest pain or breathlessness
Swelling with a sudden severe headache, vision changes or pain under the ribs in pregnancy
urgentFlags: Swelling in one leg only, especially with pain, warmth or redness in the calf
Swelling that is getting worse quickly
Swelling with breathlessness when lying down or doing light activity
Swelling with red, hot, painful skin or a high temperature
Sudden swelling of the face, hands or feet in pregnancy

commonCauses.title: Standing or sitting for long periods
commonCauses.detail: Including long flights; fluid collects in the legs.

commonCauses.title: Hot weather or pregnancy
commonCauses.detail: Mild swelling is very common in both.

commonCauses.title: Medicines
commonCauses.detail: Some blood pressure medicines, steroids and anti-inflammatories cause swelling.

commonCauses.title: Injury
commonCauses.detail: A sprain or strain causes swelling around the injured area.

commonCauses.title: Heart, kidney, liver or vein problems, or a blood clot
commonCauses.detail: Less common causes that need assessment.

selfCare: Raise your legs on a pillow when lying down
Walk regularly to improve blood flow
Wear wide, comfortable shoes
Avoid sitting or standing still for long periods
avoid: Wearing tight clothing or socks that leave marks
Sitting with your legs crossed for long periods
Diuretic ('water') tablets or herbal products without medical advice
seeDoctorIf: Swelling has not improved after 3 days of self-care
Swelling keeps coming back
You have heart, kidney or liver disease
Skin over the swelling is changing colour or becoming tight and shiny

name: Calf pain or swelling in one leg
summary: Calf pain is often a muscle strain or cramp, but pain with swelling and warmth in one leg can be a blood clot (DVT), which needs same-day assessment.
redFlags: Calf pain or swelling with sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing up blood
A cold, pale, numb or very painful leg
urgentFlags: Throbbing or cramping pain with swelling in one leg, usually the calf or thigh
Warm, red or darkened skin over the painful area
Calf pain after recent surgery, a long journey, a period of immobility, or during pregnancy or after birth
Swollen veins that are hard or sore when touched

commonCauses.title: Muscle strain or cramp
commonCauses.detail: Pain after exercise or a sudden movement, without major swelling.

commonCauses.title: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
commonCauses.detail: A blood clot in a deep vein; risk is higher after surgery, long journeys, in pregnancy, or with some contraceptive pills.

commonCauses.title: Baker's cyst
commonCauses.detail: A fluid-filled swelling behind the knee that can burst and cause calf pain.

commonCauses.title: Poor circulation
commonCauses.detail: Cramping pain when walking that eases with rest, more common in smokers.

selfCare: If a clot is possible, get medical advice the same day before doing anything else
For a clear muscle strain, rest, apply a cold pack and raise the leg
Paracetamol can ease pain, following the pack instructions
avoid: Massaging a calf that might have a blood clot
Ignoring one-sided calf swelling
seeDoctorIf: Calf pain has not improved after 2 weeks
You get pain in your calves when walking that eases when you stop
Calf pain keeps coming back

name: Foot pain
summary: Foot pain is often caused by ill-fitting shoes, overuse or minor injuries, and usually improves within 2 weeks with rest and better footwear.
redFlags: A foot that is cold, pale or blue with severe pain
Severe pain after an injury with a foot that has changed shape, or being unable to walk
A red, hot, swollen foot with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: Being unable to put weight on your foot after an injury
A red, hot, swollen foot or toe
Foot pain with tingling or numbness that is spreading
Foot pain, a wound or skin change if you have diabetes

commonCauses.title: Ill-fitting shoes and overuse
commonCauses.detail: Tight or high-heeled shoes and lots of standing or running.

commonCauses.title: Plantar fasciitis
commonCauses.detail: Pain under the heel or arch, worst with the first steps in the morning.

commonCauses.title: Bunions and toe problems
commonCauses.detail: A bony lump at the base of the big toe, or curled toes.

commonCauses.title: Sprains, strains or stress fractures
commonCauses.detail: Pain after injury or a big increase in activity.

commonCauses.title: Gout or arthritis
commonCauses.detail: Sudden severe pain in the big toe joint, or ongoing joint pain.

selfCare: Rest and raise your foot when you can
Use a cold pack wrapped in a towel for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours
Wear wide, comfortable shoes with a low heel and soft sole
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Use soft insoles or pads in your shoes
avoid: Walking or standing for long periods
High heels and tight, pointy shoes
Walking barefoot on hard surfaces
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
Pain is severe or stops you doing normal activities
You have a bunion or toe problem that is getting worse
You have diabetes and any foot problem

name: Heel pain
aliases: pain in heel in the morning
summary: Heel pain is common and is often caused by plantar fasciitis, an irritated band of tissue under the foot. It usually improves with rest, stretching and good footwear, but can take weeks to months.
redFlags: A sudden snap or pop at the back of the ankle with being unable to push off or stand on tiptoe
urgentFlags: Heel pain with numbness or tingling in the foot
A red, hot, swollen heel with a high temperature
Severe heel pain after an injury or fall from a height

commonCauses.title: Plantar fasciitis
commonCauses.detail: Pain under the heel that is worst with the first steps in the morning or after resting.

commonCauses.title: Achilles tendinopathy
commonCauses.detail: Pain and stiffness at the back of the heel, often in runners.

commonCauses.title: Achilles tendon rupture
commonCauses.detail: A sudden pain and snap at the back of the ankle; needs urgent treatment.

commonCauses.title: Stress fracture
commonCauses.detail: Pain that gets worse with activity after a big increase in exercise.

selfCare: Rest and raise your foot, and use a cold pack wrapped in a towel
Wear shoes with cushioned heels and good arch support
Do gentle calf and foot stretches daily
Use heel pads or insoles
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
avoid: Walking barefoot on hard surfaces
Standing for long periods
High heels or flat, unsupportive shoes such as flip-flops
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks of self-care
Pain is severe or affects daily activities
You have diabetes

name: Sprained or twisted ankle
summary: Sprains and strains are injuries to ligaments and muscles, often in the ankle, wrist or knee. Most get better within a few weeks with rest and gradual return to activity.
redFlags: A joint or bone that looks deformed or is sticking through the skin
A foot or hand below the injury that is cold, pale, blue or numb
A crack or snap heard at the time of injury with severe pain
urgentFlags: Being unable to put weight on the leg or use the limb
Severe pain that is not eased by painkillers
Swelling and bruising that is getting much worse
Tenderness directly over a bone

commonCauses.title: Ligament sprain
commonCauses.detail: Overstretching or tearing of a ligament, most often by rolling the ankle.

commonCauses.title: Muscle strain
commonCauses.detail: Overstretching or tearing of muscle fibres during sport or lifting.

commonCauses.title: Broken bone
commonCauses.detail: Can look similar to a sprain; severe pain, being unable to bear weight or tenderness over the bone suggest a fracture.

selfCare: Rest the injured area for the first 2 to 3 days
Apply a cold pack wrapped in a towel for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours
Raise the injured area on a pillow as often as you can
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Start gentle movement after 2 to 3 days and build up gradually
avoid: Heat, alcohol, running and massage for the first 3 days
Putting ice directly on the skin
Returning to sport too quickly
seeDoctorIf: The injury has not improved after a week of self-care
The joint keeps giving way
Pain or swelling is getting worse after the first few days

name: Hand or wrist pain
summary: Hand and wrist pain is often caused by repetitive movements, strains or arthritis, and usually improves within a few weeks.
redFlags: A hand or wrist that looks deformed after a fall or injury
A hand or fingers that are cold, pale, blue or numb after an injury
Sudden weakness or numbness of one hand with face drooping or slurred speech
urgentFlags: Severe pain or swelling after a fall onto an outstretched hand
A red, hot, swollen hand or finger, especially after a cut or bite
Being unable to move or straighten a finger after an injury

commonCauses.title: Repetitive strain
commonCauses.detail: Typing, using tools or phones, or sports.

commonCauses.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
commonCauses.detail: Tingling, numbness and pain in the thumb and fingers, often worse at night.

commonCauses.title: Osteoarthritis
commonCauses.detail: Pain and stiffness at the base of the thumb or finger joints.

commonCauses.title: Tendon problems
commonCauses.detail: Pain at the base of the thumb, or a finger that catches or locks.

commonCauses.title: Broken wrist
commonCauses.detail: After a fall onto the hand; can look like a sprain.

selfCare: Rest from activities that cause pain
Use a cold pack wrapped in a towel for swelling
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, or use an anti-inflammatory gel, following the pack instructions
A wrist splint at night can help tingling from carpal tunnel syndrome
Gently move the joints to keep them from getting stiff
avoid: Repetitive gripping or typing without breaks
Heavy lifting with the painful hand
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
You have tingling or numbness that does not go away
Your hand is weak or you keep dropping things
A finger keeps locking or catching

name: Elbow and arm pain
summary: Elbow and arm pain is usually caused by overuse, such as tennis elbow, and gets better with rest and time.
redFlags: Arm pain with chest pain, breathlessness, sweating or feeling sick
An arm or elbow that looks deformed after an injury
Sudden weakness or numbness of the arm with face drooping or slurred speech
urgentFlags: Being unable to move the elbow or arm after an injury
A red, hot, swollen elbow, especially with a high temperature
Pain with tingling or numbness that is not going away

commonCauses.title: Tennis or golfer's elbow
commonCauses.detail: Pain on the outside or inside of the elbow from overuse of forearm muscles.

commonCauses.title: Bursitis
commonCauses.detail: A soft swelling at the back of the elbow.

commonCauses.title: Trapped nerve
commonCauses.detail: Tingling in the arm or fingers from a nerve in the neck or elbow.

commonCauses.title: Injury
commonCauses.detail: Sprains, dislocations or broken bones after a fall.

selfCare: Rest the arm and avoid the activity that causes pain
Use a cold pack wrapped in a towel
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, or use an anti-inflammatory gel, following the pack instructions
Gently stretch and strengthen the forearm as pain eases
avoid: Repetitive gripping or lifting with the painful arm
Keeping the arm completely still for a long time
seeDoctorIf: Pain has not improved after 2 weeks
You have tingling, numbness or weakness in your hand
Pain is affecting work or sleep

name: Possible broken bone
summary: A broken bone usually causes pain, swelling and difficulty using the injured part. Most need an X-ray; a broken toe or finger may be managed more simply.
redFlags: A bone sticking out through the skin, or a limb at an odd angle
Heavy bleeding from the injury
A limb below the injury that is cold, pale, blue or numb
A suspected broken hip, leg, pelvis, neck or back
An injury to the head, neck or back with numbness, tingling or weakness
urgentFlags: Pain, swelling and bruising after a fall, with difficulty using the limb
Tenderness directly over a bone
A snap or grinding noise at the time of the injury
A suspected broken wrist, arm or ankle

commonCauses.title: Falls and sports injuries
commonCauses.detail: The most common causes, especially falling onto an outstretched hand.

commonCauses.title: Osteoporosis
commonCauses.detail: Thin bones break more easily, often after a minor fall in older people.

commonCauses.title: Overuse
commonCauses.detail: Stress fractures from repeated impact, such as running.

selfCare: Keep the injured part still and supported while getting help
Apply a cold pack wrapped in a towel to reduce swelling
Take paracetamol for pain, following the pack instructions
Do not eat or drink if you have a serious injury, in case you need an operation
For a suspected broken toe, rest, raise the foot and wear stiff, wide shoes
avoid: Trying to straighten or push a bone back into place
Moving someone with a suspected neck or back injury unless they are in danger
Walking on a leg that might be broken
seeDoctorIf: A suspected broken toe is not getting better after 6 weeks
Pain or swelling after a minor injury is not improving after a few days
You have had a broken bone after a minor fall and are over 50
